name: New York Stop Hacks and Improve Electronic Data Security Act (SHIELD Act)

articles.title: Private information — expanded definition
articles.requirement: Private information includes: (i) personal information in combination with (1) Social Security number, (2) driver's license / non-driver ID, (3) financial account or credit / debit card with credentials enabling access, (4) biometric information, or (5) username / email + password / security Q&A enabling account access; (ii) username / email + password / security Q&A as a stand-alone category (account-takeover exposure). NEW (vs pre-SHIELD): biometric data + access credentials added.

articles.title: Breach notification trigger + 'access' standard
articles.requirement: Notification triggered by (a) acquisition OR (b) access — SHIELD lowered the trigger from 'acquisition' to 'access' (whether the unauthorised person actually exfiltrated data is not required). Notice to affected NY residents 'in the most expedient time possible + without unreasonable delay'. Notice to NY AG, Department of State + Division of State Police; consumer reporting agencies if > 5,000 affected. Form prescribed.

articles.title: Reasonable security — administrative safeguards
articles.requirement: Any person or business owning or licensing computerised data which includes private information of a NY resident must develop, implement + maintain reasonable safeguards. Administrative safeguards: (a) designates one or more employees to coordinate the security program; (b) identifies reasonably foreseeable internal + external risks; (c) assesses sufficiency of safeguards in place; (d) trains employees in security-program practices + procedures; (e) selects service providers capable of maintaining appropriate safeguards + requires contractual obligations; (f) adjusts program in light of business changes / new circumstances.

articles.title: Reasonable security — technical safeguards
articles.requirement: Technical safeguards: (a) assesses risks in network + software design; (b) assesses risks in information processing, transmission + storage; (c) detects, prevents + responds to attacks or system failures; (d) regularly tests + monitors effectiveness of key controls, systems + procedures.

articles.title: Reasonable security — physical safeguards
articles.requirement: Physical safeguards: (a) assesses risks of information storage + disposal; (b) detects, prevents + responds to intrusions; (c) protects against unauthorised access to or use of private information during or after collection, transportation + destruction or disposal; (d) disposes of private information within a reasonable time after it is no longer needed for business purposes by erasing electronic media so the information cannot be read or reconstructed.

articles.title: Small business proportionality
articles.requirement: Small business compliance is deemed achieved when its safeguards are reasonable + appropriate to its size + complexity + the nature + scope of its activities + the sensitivity of the personal information it handles. 'Small business' = fewer than 50 employees + less than $3m in gross annual revenue in the last 3 fiscal years OR less than $5m in year-end total assets.

articles.title: Compliance with other frameworks
articles.requirement: Compliant entities deemed compliant with SHIELD where they: (a) comply with regulations promulgated under GLBA (federal); (b) comply with HIPAA / HITECH (health data); (c) comply with NYDFS Part 500 (financial services — Covered Entities). Single-source compliance significantly reduces SHIELD burden for NYDFS-regulated entities. Enforcement: NY AG actions for civil monetary penalties; per-instance penalties up to $20 per failed notice + $250,000 cap (breach notice) + per-incident reasonable-security penalties up to $5,000.
